Main Points
⏺ Cryptocurrency and blockchain technology are being explored as solutions for secure and transparent online voting systems.
⏺ Blockchain provides immutability, security, and verifiability for election processes.
⏺ This post explores how cryptocurrencies and blockchain are shaping the future of voting and elections.

1️⃣ Blockchain for Transparent Voting: Blockchain ensures that every vote is securely recorded and cannot be altered or tampered with, offering a transparent election process.
2️⃣ Privacy and Security in Voting: Cryptocurrencies and blockchain can enhance the privacy of voters, ensuring that personal data is encrypted and protected from unauthorized access.
3️⃣ Cost-Effective Solutions: Blockchain voting systems can reduce the costs associated with traditional voting methods, such as paper ballots, transportation, and polling staff.
4️⃣ Increased Voter Accessibility: Cryptocurrencies enable secure voting from any location with an internet connection, increasing voter participation in local, regional, and national elections.
5️⃣ The Future of Blockchain Voting: As blockchain technology matures, it could become the standard for elections worldwide, offering a more secure, efficient, and transparent method of voting.

Final Thoughts

Blockchain and cryptocurrency have the potential to revolutionize the way we vote, making elections more secure, transparent, and accessible. As technology continues to evolve, blockchain-based voting could become the standard for democratic participation.

🔔 Ethereum price holds above $1,750 after 12% rally as bulls battle key resistance 

🔖 Ethereum has climbed about 12% since July 1 as weaker-than-expected U.S. employment data and renewed institutional inflows pushed buyers back into the market, although the asset now faces heavy resistance near the $1,800 level. Ethereum’s rally gathered pace after the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that June nonfarm payrolls rose by just 57,000, far below expectations of roughly 115,000. Treasury yields also eased following the release, giving cryptocurrencies another tailwind as investors rotated back into higher-beta assets.

⚠️ Ethereum’s own fundamentals strengthened alongside the macro backdrop. On July 1, Ethereum Institutional launched with backing from ecosystem leaders including co-founder Joe Lubin to accelerate institutional adoption of the network. A day later, U.S. spot Ethereum ETFs reversed an eight-week streak of net outflows, attracting $29.1 million in fresh capital led by BlackRock’s ETHA. The return of positive ETF flows removed a persistent source of selling pressure that had weighed on ETH throughout the second quarter. 

🌐 Ethereum entered the rebound from deeply oversold conditions after closing its first-ever stretch of three consecutive losing quarters. The correction dragged ETH from above $3,400 to nearly $1,563 by July 1 while active network addresses fell roughly 46%, leaving market positioning heavily skewed toward bearish bets before buyers regained control. The daily chart shows ETH reclaiming the 0.786 Fibonacci retracement near $1,704 after bouncing from the $1,500 region. Price is also pressing against the daily Supertrend resistance around $1,807 while remaining beneath a descending trendline that has capped every rally since May.

In March, a member of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps was convicted in the US of a murder-for-hire plot targeting politicians, including Trump.

Asif Merchant, an Iranian intelligence official, was arrested after allegedly meeting with hitmen – who were in fact undercover agents – in New York in June 2024, according to the US department of justice.

Tehran has been mourning Ali Khamenei, its supreme leader, who was killed during the first round of US strikes in February and whose funeral has taken place in recent days.

The ceremonies also included effigies of the US president and an enormous banner in Qom promising a $100m bounty for his murder.

The coffin was interred at the Imam Reza shrine in Mashhad, Khamenei’s birthplace, after a funeral prayer before large crowds.

Iran state media said that up to 43 million people attended the six-day ceremony, calling it “the largest procession the world has ever witnessed”.

However, US strikes on Iran delayed the burial earlier in the day. The final procession was scheduled to take place at 8am local time (5.30am BST) on Thursday, but was pushed back by eight hours.

US-Israel relations under strain
The United States and Iran have resumed a new wave of tit-for-tat strikes after Iran targeted three tankers in the Strait of Hormuz.

Trump declared the US-Iran ceasefire to be over during the Nato summit in Turkey, as the US Central Command said its forces had struck approximately 90 military targets in the country.

Iran responded by targeting US military bases across the Middle East on Thursday.

Relations between Trump and Benjamin Netanyahu, the Israeli prime minister, have also apparently become strained since the two countries embarked on their conflict with Iran.

Mr Netanyahu has pushed for the conflict to continue, while Trump, facing criticism over the war, even from some factions of his own party, has sought to bring it to an end.

The pair spoke on Thursday, according to The Wall Street Journal, during which they agreed to continue “coordination between the countries”, the Israeli prime minister’s office said.

“As part of the continuous contact” between the two, “President Trump updated the prime minister on American moves in the Gulf,” the Israeli leader’s office said.
